source.repository: external: numpy/numpy (https://github.com/numpy/numpy), cloned locally for this review

groundTruth.description: Fixes CVE-2014-1858/GHSA-cw6w-4rcx-xphc: numpy.f2py.compile() and the f2py CLI's --build-dir default used tempfile.mktemp(), which only returns a filename that a local attacker can race to replace with a symlink before the caller opens/creates it (a classic TOCTOU symlink attack enabling arbitrary file write). The fix replaces mktemp()-then-open with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() (atomic create) in __init__.py's compile(), and tempfile.mkdtemp() (atomic directory create) for the CLI's build-dir default in f2py2e.py. First data-science-domain case in the corpus (prior cases are all web/backend/CLI tooling).

evidence.note: mktemp()+open replaced by NamedTemporaryFile(), written/flushed/closed in a try/finally
build_dir default switched from mktemp() to mkdtemp()

groundTruth.confirmingFix: this commit itself; see GHSA-cw6w-4rcx-xphc / CVE-2014-1858

runs.label: live run, Claude Code CLI 2.1.299, external repository input, maxInputTokensPerReviewer 150000, context-window 250000

dispositions.note: Verified by direct execution: `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.f')` defaults to binary mode ('w+b'); running `f.write(source)` with a str argument against it raises `TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'` under Python 3 (reproduced directly, not inferred). The file does declare `from __future__ import ... print_function`, consistent with dual Python 2/3 targeting at this point in numpy's history. This is a real, change-introduced functional regression: the OLD code's equivalent path used `open(fname, 'w')` (text mode), so it worked; the NEW code's `source_fn is None` branch switched to NamedTemporaryFile's binary default while the `source_fn` branch right next to it still uses `open(source_fn, 'w')` (text mode) - the finding's own observation that "the two branches behave differently" is accurate. The security fix (replacing a symlink-race-prone mktemp() with an atomic create) is itself sound; this is an independent, genuine bug introduced alongside it in the same commit, not a restatement of the CVE this change fixes.

notes:
The real commit also touched three test files (test_memmap.py, test_multiarray.py, test_io.py) adjusting assertions for the new temp-file behavior; excluded from the reviewed diff since they're test-only follow-on and not part of the security-relevant change itself.

This case did not come back clean as the groundTruth's expectedVerdict anticipated (patterned on the historical CVE fix alone) - the live run surfaced a real, confirmed-by-execution Required finding unrelated to the CVE being fixed: a Python-3 binary-vs-text temp-file mode regression introduced in the same commit. Left as-is rather than retroactively rewritten, consistent with how this corpus handles a groundTruth description that turns out to be incomplete once a run actually happens (see also case 013's notes on the same point).
